note: Register of tabnas runtime dependencies that differ between this repository's ports (tabnas/admin ADR-24). tools/port-deps.cjs fails on a difference that is not listed here, and on an entry that no longer matches the manifests, so the list cannot outlive what it records. Every entry states the ports that have the dependency today, the reason, and the repair.

parser.reason: TypeScript: ts/src/yaml.ts has `import { Tabnas } from '@tabnas/parser'`, a value import (`new Tabnas().use(jsonic)` parses `grammarText` in `Yaml`), and a second import from the same package of `Rule`, `RuleSpec`, `Plugin`, `Config`, `TabnasOptions`, `Context`, `Lex` and `Token`, all types; ts/package.json lists @tabnas/parser in peerDependencies. Rust: `use tabnas::{...}` in rs/src/lib.rs, lex.rs, state.rs and text.rs, and `pub use tabnas::TabnasError as YamlError` in lib.rs, with `tabnas` (package tabnas-parser) in [dependencies] of rs/Cargo.toml. Go: no non-test .go file under go/ imports github.com/tabnas/parser/go; go/yaml.go imports no tabnas module but github.com/tabnas/jsonic/go. Where TypeScript constructs the engine itself, yaml.go gets one from jsonic's own `Make` (in `MakeJsonic`, and in `configureGrammarRules` to parse `grammarText`), and names the engine's types through the aliases in jsonic's go/engine.go (`jsonic.Jsonic`, `jsonic.Rule`, `jsonic.Context`, `jsonic.Tin`, `jsonic.Token`, `jsonic.OrderedMap`). go/go.mod requires the parser directly only because two test files import it: go/key_before_value_test.go (`tabnas.Rule`, `tabnas.Context`, `tabnas.RuleDone`, `tabnas.OPEN`) and go/parity_regression_test.go (`tabnas.OrderedMap`).
parser.repair: To agree on having it: go/yaml.go would import github.com/tabnas/parser/go for the engine types it now takes from jsonic; go/go.mod already requires it directly. To agree on not having it: ts/src/yaml.ts would take `Tabnas`, and the types `Rule`, `RuleSpec`, `Config`, `Context`, `Lex` and `Token`, from @tabnas/jsonic, which re-exports them under the same names (jsonic's ts/src/jsonic.ts), `TabnasOptions` under the name `Options` (jsonic's ts/src/types.ts), and the engine's `Plugin` under the name `TabnasPlugin` (`export type { Plugin as TabnasPlugin } from '@tabnas/parser'`), because jsonic's own `Plugin` type is a different one whose first argument is a `Jsonic` instance; ts/package.json would then drop the @tabnas/parser peer. In Rust that move is not available today: tabnas-jsonic re-exports only `TabnasError` (as `JsonicError`), so jsonic's rs/src/lib.rs would first have to re-export the engine's items before rs/src here could take them from it and rs/Cargo.toml drop `tabnas` from [dependencies]. Either way the engine stays in every port's build, because jsonic depends on it in all three (peerDependencies of its ts/package.json, the import in its go/engine.go, [dependencies] of its rs/Cargo.toml). Undecided: awaits the maintainer's ruling.
